entry_point.code: static inline const char* DecodeEntry(const char* p, const char* limit,

trace.code: if (static_cast<uint32_t>(limit - p) < (*non_shared + *value_length)) { return nullptr; }  // uint32 addition overflows: non_shared=1 + value_length=0xffffffff wraps to 0, so 'remaining < 0' is always false and the bounds check is bypassed
key_.append(p, non_shared); value_ = Slice(p + non_shared, value_length);  // value Slice is built from the attacker-controlled length (0xffffffff) with no re-check
std::string ToString() const { return std::string(data_, size_); }  // consuming the value copies size_ bytes -> up to 4 GiB out-of-bounds read
if (static_cast<uint32_t>(limit - p) < *non_shared || static_cast<uint32_t>(limit - p) - *non_shared < *value_length) { return nullptr; }  // two-step check cannot wrap

preconditions: A LevelDB-backed application opens an SSTable (.ldb/.sst) whose block entries are attacker-influenced (a downloaded/shared/synced database file, a game save, a cache the attacker can write)
The application iterates or Get()s the corrupted key so that Block::Iter::ParseNextKey decodes the malformed entry and the caller consumes the returned value
Google leveldb release 1.23 (Feb 2021) or earlier — the fix (29465588d3, Nov 2026) is unreleased

evidence.vulnerable_version: google/leveldb 1.23 (2021-02-23) and earlier, including current master prior to 29465588d3
evidence.observed_result: Faithful C++ reproduction of table/block.cc DecodeEntry (vulnerable vs fixed) compiled with zig c++. A corrupt block entry (shared=0, non_shared=1, value_length=0xffffffff, 1 key byte — the exact bytes of the upstream CorruptedBlockEntryLengthOverflow regression test) makes the vulnerable 'remaining < (non_shared + value_length)' check wrap (1 + 0xffffffff == 0) and pass, so DecodeEntry returns non-null and the iterator yields a value Slice of size 0xffffffff (4 GiB) with 0 bytes of actual data remaining. The fixed two-step check returns nullptr (corruption).

real_exploit.target: google/leveldb table/block.cc DecodeEntry @ bb74ef73 (release 1.23) vs fix 29465588d3
real_exploit.backend: faithful C++ reproduction of the vulnerable/fixed DecodeEntry + Slice (exact logic from table/block.cc, util/coding.cc, include/leveldb/slice.h), compiled and executed natively
real_exploit.marker: RESULT: INTEGER OVERFLOW -> OOB READ CONFIRMED
real_exploit.demonstrated: The 32-bit addition non_shared + value_length wraps to 0 (CWE-190), bypassing the bounds check, so a corrupt block entry produces a 0xffffffff-byte value Slice (CWE-125 OOB read of up to 4 GiB past the block). The fixed code detects the corruption and returns nullptr.
